Phoenix.name: House of the Phoenix
Phoenix.description: You are, it would seem, of House Phoenix! This House—which has, throughout the long turning of the Cycle, provided the Empire with rulers of vision and principle—is distinguished by an unwavering commitment to justice that transcends mere legal formality, and by a concern for mystical truths and higher purposes that others, perhaps less attuned to such matters, might dismiss as impractical idealism. The Phoenix demonstrates, if we may be permitted to observe, a marked tendency to view situations through the lens of moral imperatives rather than expedient calculations, and has shown throughout history a willingness to challenge established authority when perceiving it to be unjust—rising, as their symbol suggests most aptly, from circumstances that would crush lesser spirits. Critics have occasionally described the Phoenix as excessively idealistic or insufficiently practical; their defenders counter, with considerable justice, that civilization requires those willing to stand for what is right regardless of personal consequence, and that today's impractical idealism often becomes tomorrow's established justice.

Dragon.name: House of the Dragon
Dragon.description: You are, beyond question, of House Dragon! This House—which has provided the Empire with its finest military commanders and most decisive leaders since time immemorial—is characterized by martial prowess, strategic acumen, and an instinctive understanding of hierarchy, command, and the clear exercise of authority. The Dragon places great emphasis on discipline, direct action, and the value of decisions made boldly and executed without hesitation. Their conception of honor is straightforward and martial—tested on the battlefield rather than debated in philosophical discourse—and their natural confidence and commanding presence often lead others to follow their leadership even in circumstances where formal authority might be, shall we say, ambiguous. While some have characterized the House as excessively aggressive or overly fond of military solutions to problems that might admit of other approaches, the Dragon's defenders point out, with considerable merit, that the Empire's stability has often depended upon precisely the sort of decisive action that this House provides instinctively and without the paralyzing hesitation that afflicts lesser spirits.

Lyorn.name: House of the Lyorn
Lyorn.description: You are, it appears, of House Lyorn! This House—which serves as guardian of tradition and keeper of proper forms within Dragaeran society—is distinguished by meticulous observance of custom, unwavering adherence to codes of honor, and a firm conviction that civilization depends upon the preservation of accumulated wisdom passed down through generations uncounted. The Lyorn demonstrates extraordinary reliability—a Lyorn's word, once given, may be considered as absolute as the rotation of the Cycle itself—and shows particular concern for propriety and correct conduct, understanding, as perhaps others do not, that rituals and traditions serve purposes beyond mere formality. Their approach to honor is both comprehensive and exacting, encompassing not merely grand gestures—though the Lyorn is certainly capable of such—but the daily practice of correct behavior in all circumstances, however humble. While critics have sometimes characterized the House as inflexible or overly concerned with formality at the expense of practical effectiveness, the Lyorn maintains, with unshakeable conviction, that without such adherence to principle and tradition, society loses the very foundations that distinguish civilization from barbarism.

Tiassa.name: House of the Tiassa
Tiassa.description: You are, most assuredly, of House Tiassa! This House—noted throughout the Empire for producing individuals of remarkable cleverness, creativity, and adaptability—approaches problems with imagination rather than force, preferring elegant solutions to brute-force methods, and demonstrating a marked tendency toward unconventional thinking that permits the perception of opportunities where others see only obstacles. Historical records contain numerous accounts—which this historian has examined personally, and can therefore attest to their veracity—of Tiassa nobles achieving their objectives through wit, ingenuity, and the creative application of available resources rather than through direct confrontation or the tedious accumulation of superior force. The House has produced many of the Empire's finest storytellers, strategists, and innovators—individuals capable of connecting disparate concepts in unexpected ways that leave more linear thinkers bewildered by the very brilliance of the approach. While some have characterized the House as excessively unconventional or insufficiently respectful of tradition, the Tiassa maintains, with characteristic wit, that creativity and adaptability are essential virtues in a changing world, and that rigid adherence to established methods produces rigid and unsatisfactory results.

Athyra.name: House of the Athyra
Athyra.description: You are, beyond any doubt, of House Athyra! This House—long associated with scholarship, sorcerous research, and the systematic pursuit of knowledge in all its manifestations—demonstrates an insatiable intellectual curiosity and a conviction, shared by all true scholars, that understanding represents the highest form of achievement. The Athyra has produced many of the Empire's most accomplished sorcerers, scholars, and natural philosophers, and their methodology is characterized by patience, systematic investigation, and rigorous logical analysis applied with the precision of a master craftsman. Members of this House pursue knowledge not merely for practical application—though such applications often follow, as night follows day—but for its intrinsic value, believing, as this historian does, that understanding itself justifies the effort of acquisition. While critics have occasionally characterized the Athyra as overly cerebral or detached from practical concerns—a criticism that reveals more about the critic than the subject—the House maintains that today's theoretical knowledge becomes tomorrow's practical application, and that many of the Empire's most significant magical and philosophical advances bear the unmistakable mark of Athyra scholarship and patience.

Issola.name: House of the Issola
Issola.description: You are, it would appear, of House Issola! This House—recognized throughout the Empire as master of diplomacy, courtesy, and the subtle arts of social navigation—demonstrates extraordinary grace in all interactions, possessing what might appear to the uninitiated as an almost supernatural ability to perceive unspoken meanings and navigate complex social situations with the ease of a skilled sailor navigating familiar waters. The Issola has provided the Empire with its finest ambassadors, mediators, and courtiers—individuals capable of forging agreement between parties who seemed, to less skilled observers, irreconcilably opposed. Their methodology emphasizes indirect influence over direct command, understanding over confrontation, and the careful management of relationships and perceptions in a manner that makes difficult negotiations appear effortless. While some have mistaken Issola courtesy for weakness or their diplomacy for indecisiveness—errors that reveal only the observer's failure to understand that true power often operates most effectively when least visible—the House maintains, with characteristic grace, that civilization's greatest achievements occur not through force but through the patient building of consensus and cooperation.

Yendi.name: House of the Yendi
Yendi.description: You are, it seems, of House Yendi! This House—renowned for strategic thinking, intelligence gathering, and the ability to perceive patterns and connections that remain invisible to those less gifted in such perception—approaches situations with careful analysis, always seeking to understand underlying motivations and hidden relationships that others, perhaps less patient or less perceptive, might overlook entirely. The Yendi demonstrates particular excellence in planning, information analysis, and the identification of optimal courses of action among multiple alternatives—a skill that has, on numerous occasions documented in the historical record, permitted Yendi nobles to achieve their objectives well before others realized that a contest had even occurred. The House places great value on information—its gathering, its analysis, and its strategic application—and their methodology emphasizes preparation, contingency planning, and the careful positioning of oneself advantageously before any actual confrontation becomes necessary. While critics have sometimes characterized the House as excessively cautious or overly fond of complexity where simplicity might suffice, the Yendi maintains that direct confrontation is often unnecessary when superior positioning and better information are available to those wise enough to acquire them.

Jhereg.name: House of the Jhereg
Jhereg.description: You are, without question, of House Jhereg! This House—which occupies a unique position within the Empire, being the only House that accepts members by purchase rather than birth—is characterized by pragmatism, organizational skill, and an unflinching realistic assessment of situations as they actually exist rather than as others, perhaps more comfortable with pleasant fictions, might wish them to be. The Jhereg demonstrates remarkable flexibility, being unconstrained by traditional notions of honor or propriety when such constraints would interfere with practical objectives—a trait that more conventional Houses find either admirably pragmatic or deeply troubling, depending upon their own philosophical inclinations. Their methodology emphasizes efficiency, profit, and the identification of opportunities that others overlook or consider beneath their dignity, and the House has developed sophisticated organizational structures that would, if we are honest, earn admiration in any legitimate enterprise. While the Jhereg's involvement in activities of questionable legality is well documented—indeed, the House makes no particular effort to conceal such involvement—they maintain, with considerable logic, that they provide services for which there is genuine demand and that hypocrisy lies in condemning what one secretly patronizes.

Orca.name: House of the Orca
Orca.description: You are, it appears, of House Orca! This House—which has long dominated Imperial commerce, trade, and economic affairs with a skill that even their rivals must acknowledge—demonstrates exceptional ability in negotiation, an instinctive understanding of value and exchange, and the capacity to structure agreements beneficial to all parties involved, or at the very least, beneficial to themselves. The Orca approaches situations through the lens of transaction and mutual benefit, perceiving the world as a vast network of exchanges and relationships where everything possesses value and everything, given sufficient creativity in negotiation, may be obtained. Their methodology emphasizes the building of commercial networks, the establishment of reputation as reliable trading partners, and the skillful assessment of what others want and what they will pay to obtain it—skills that have made the Orca, collectively, among the wealthiest individuals in the Empire. While some noble Houses affect to disdain commerce as beneath their dignity—an affectation that this historian finds both amusing and somewhat hypocritical—the Orca points out that everyone engages in exchange and that skill in this arena deserves recognition rather than dismissal born of aristocratic pretension.

Dzur.name: House of the Dzur
Dzur.description: You are, beyond all doubt, of House Dzur! This House—legendary throughout the Empire for physical courage carried to lengths that others find incomprehensible or, to speak plainly, terrifying—faces danger not merely without fear but with active enthusiasm, seeking out challenges that would cause more prudent individuals to retreat with all possible speed. The Dzur defines honor in the most direct possible terms—as the courage to do what is right regardless of personal risk or consequence—and their methodology eschews subtlety, deception, and careful calculation in favor of direct confrontation and immediate action. Historical records contain numerous accounts—verified by this historian through extensive research—of Dzur nobles achieving victory through sheer courage and determination in situations where any rational assessment would have counseled immediate withdrawal, if not outright flight. While critics characterize the House as reckless or lacking in strategic sophistication—criticisms that the Dzur receives with magnificent indifference—the House maintains that there exist things worth dying for and that life without honor and courage is scarcely worth living. The Empire has benefited immeasurably from Dzur courage, particularly in circumstances requiring someone willing to face impossible odds without hesitation.

Jhegaala.name: House of the Jhegaala
Jhegaala.description: You are, it seems, of House Jhegaala! This House—perhaps the most enigmatic of the noble Houses, and certainly the most difficult for this historian to characterize with any confidence—is distinguished by an extraordinary capacity for adaptation and transformation that other Houses find both fascinating and somewhat unsettling. Jhegaala nobles demonstrate an unusual flexibility of character and approach, capable of reinventing themselves as circumstances demand, and show little attachment to fixed identity or rigid principle, preferring instead to flow like water into whatever form serves current purposes. This adaptability manifests in unconventional thinking, willingness to abandon approaches that no longer serve, and an openness to possibilities that more tradition-bound Houses cannot even perceive, much less pursue. While critics sometimes characterize the Jhegaala as inconsistent or lacking in principle—a criticism that assumes principle requires rigidity, which this historian questions—the House maintains that rigidity is weakness and that survival and success belong to those capable of learning, growing, and changing as circumstances require. The Jhegaala's contributions to Imperial culture are difficult to categorize, which is perhaps entirely appropriate for a House that resists categorization as a matter of fundamental philosophy.

Chreotha.name: House of the Chreotha
Chreotha.description: You are, without doubt, of House Chreotha! This House—characterized by patience, careful observation, and an understanding that success often belongs not to the swift but to the persistent—demonstrates exceptional skill in the long pursuit and the patient identification of opportunity. Chreotha nobles possess a remarkable capacity for sustained effort and focused attention over extended periods, combined with an instinct for timing that permits them to act decisively when the moment is right. The House's methodology emphasizes careful observation of patterns, patient accumulation of advantage, and the wisdom to recognize that many objectives cannot be rushed but must be approached with the same patience a hunter demonstrates when tracking worthy prey. While other Houses may celebrate bold action and immediate results, the Chreotha understands that some things ripen in their own time and that premature action often destroys what patient waiting would have secured. Historical records show that while the Chreotha may not produce as many celebrated heroes as other Houses—heroes being, after all, often distinguished by dramatic and immediate action—their members demonstrate remarkable success through patient, persistent effort. The House maintains that there is considerable satisfaction in the successful conclusion of a long pursuit, and that immediate gratification is often the enemy of lasting achievement.

Teckla.name: House of the Teckla
Teckla.description: You are, it appears, of House Teckla! This House—the largest of the noble Houses and, if we are honest, the essential foundation upon which all of Dragaeran civilization rests—demonstrates exceptional perseverance, practical skill, and the ability to endure circumstances that would break more celebrated but less resilient individuals. The Teckla provides the Empire with its farmers, craftspeople, laborers, and the vast apparatus of daily work that maintains civilization, performing tasks that other Houses consider beneath their dignity but which are, nonetheless, absolutely essential. While other Houses may concern themselves with grand strategy, philosophical discourse, or martial glory, the Teckla quietly maintains the daily work of civilization—and demonstrates, if one observes carefully, a strength that lies not in dramatic gestures but in the ability to continue, day after day, performing necessary labor regardless of circumstances or recognition. The House's methodology emphasizes practical skill, steady effort, and resilience—qualities that lack the drama of heroic combat or brilliant strategy but which prove, in the long term, perhaps more essential to survival and success. The Empire would collapse within weeks without Teckla labor, a fact that other Houses sometimes forget but which the Cycle itself acknowledges through the Teckla's inevitable return to ascendance.

Tsalmoth.name: House of the Tsalmoth
Tsalmoth.description: You are, beyond question, of House Tsalmoth! This House—which combines martial excellence with a strict code of honor in a manner that distinguishes it from other martially-inclined Houses—produces warriors who are both formidable in combat and principled in conduct. The Tsalmoth demonstrates courage and martial skill comparable to the Dzur, but tempered with discipline and a conviction that how one fights matters as much as whether one wins, and that certain methods remain unacceptable regardless of potential military advantage. Their methodology emphasizes training, discipline, and the development of martial skill within a framework of honorable conduct—a combination that some other Houses find admirable and others find impractical, depending upon their own philosophical inclinations regarding the relationship between honor and effectiveness. The House produces warriors who respect worthy opponents, disdain those who fight dishonorably, and believe that the battlefield serves as a proving ground where true character reveals itself. While critics sometimes suggest that the Tsalmoth's code of honor represents an impractical constraint in actual warfare—where, they argue, victory should be pursued by whatever means prove effective—the House maintains that honor distinguishes the warrior from the mere killer and that victory without honor is hollow, a position that has earned them considerable respect even from those who question its practical wisdom.

Vallista.name: House of the Vallista
Vallista.description: You are, it would seem, of House Vallista! This House—distinguished by craftsmanship, patience, and the creation of works intended to endure for generations—demonstrates exceptional skill in building, crafting, and the patient development of any project requiring sustained attention to detail and long-term planning. The Vallista approaches tasks with meticulous care, understanding that quality cannot be rushed and that the foundation determines everything that follows—a principle applicable, if we reflect upon it, to far more than merely physical construction. Their methodology emphasizes precision, proper technique, and the satisfaction of work well done rather than merely work quickly completed, and the House has provided the Empire with its finest architects, craftspeople, and builders whose creations remain functional and admired centuries after completion. While other Houses may seek immediate results or dramatic achievements that earn immediate recognition, the Vallista thinks in terms of decades and centuries, planning not for today but for the future—a perspective that this historian, whose work also contemplates the long span of years, finds particularly admirable. Critics sometimes characterize the House as slow or excessively perfectionist, but the Vallista maintains that haste produces inferior results and that true value lies in durability rather than speed, a philosophy evident in the many bridges, fortifications, and public buildings throughout the Empire that bear the unmistakable mark of Vallista craftsmanship.

Iorich.name: House of the Iorich
Iorich.description: You are, without doubt, of House Iorich! This House—which serves as guardian of justice and advocate for those requiring legal representation within the Empire—demonstrates deep commitment to legal principles, procedural fairness, and the conviction that law provides the essential framework preventing civilization from descending into rule by force alone. The Iorich distinguishes carefully between law and justice—a distinction that less thoughtful individuals sometimes fail to appreciate—and works diligently to ensure these remain aligned rather than diverging into the sort of legalistic tyranny that serves the letter while betraying the spirit. Their methodology emphasizes proper procedure, careful analysis of precedent, and meticulous adherence to legal forms—not as mere technicality, as critics sometimes suggest, but as essential safeguards protecting the weak from the powerful and ensuring that decisions rest upon principle rather than momentary passion or convenient expediency. The House has provided the Empire with its finest advocates, jurists, and legal scholars, and demonstrates particular skill in argumentation, legal analysis, and the patient pursuit of justice through proper channels. While some characterize the Iorich as excessively legalistic or overly concerned with procedure at the expense of practical results, the House maintains that how decisions are reached matters as much as the decisions themselves, and that without the rule of law, only the rule of force remains.

Hawk.name: House of the Hawk
Hawk.description: You are, it appears, of House Hawk! This House—distinguished by extraordinary perceptual abilities and an unusual capacity for noticing details that escape ordinary observation—demonstrates remarkable powers of observation, pattern recognition, and the ability to perceive significance in details that others dismiss as irrelevant or fail to notice entirely. The Hawk processes information differently than others, making connections and identifying patterns in ways that appear intuitive but reflect, upon closer examination, deep perceptual and analytical capabilities operating through mechanisms not entirely understood even by scholars who have studied the phenomenon. Their methodology emphasizes careful observation, patient analysis, and the willingness to spend substantial time simply watching and understanding before taking action—an approach that more impulsive individuals find frustrating but which consistently produces insights unavailable through more direct methods. Historical records contain numerous accounts of Hawk nobles perceiving the critical detail or recognizing the significant pattern that unlocked understanding of complex situations that had baffled others despite their possession of the same basic information. While the Hawk may appear distant or overly contemplative to those accustomed to more immediate action, this reflects not detachment but rather a different mode of engagement with reality—one that perceives what is actually present rather than what expectation suggests should be present.
